headline: You learn Rust by building things yourself, questioning the machinery underneath, and asking for feedback that sharpens your next attempt.

archetype.name: The Hands-On Investigator
archetype.description: You treat AI as a tutor and reviewer while keeping the implementation in your own hands. Your questions move from ownership and borrowing into CLI tools and browser games, with frequent stops to ask why something works, where it breaks, and whether your solution feels idiomatic. You prefer a learning loop with explanations, independent attempts, and specific feedback.

dimensions.title: Explain, try, review
dimensions.summary: You prefer guidance that leaves room for you to do the work. Across exercises, CLI development, and game mechanics, you implement a solution and then ask for a focused review.

evidence.quote: Don't write it for me, just give me the steps.
I implemented a fixed timestep with an accumulator. can you check my logic?
explain AABB first, then let me try to implement it

dimensions.title: Short questions, clear boundaries
dimensions.summary: You write brief, conversational prompts that make the next step clear. You also expose your current understanding and question trade-offs, giving the assistant something concrete to explain or challenge.

evidence.quote: I thought I only had one mutable reference.
is tokio the only option? what are the trade-offs with smol?
quiz me on Rust traits, 5 questions, wait for my answers

dimensions.title: Rust through practical projects
dimensions.summary: You describe yourself as new to Rust and use Python and JavaScript as reference points. Your exploration spans serialization, CLI tooling, async execution, and WebAssembly, with game development becoming a practical testing ground.

evidence.quote: I'm new to Rust. Can you explain ownership like I'm a Python developer?
I'm stuck on step 3, how do I serialize a Vec of structs to JSON with serde?
explain async/await in Rust vs JavaScript. why does Rust need an executor?
Can I run Rust in the browser? I want to make a small game with WebAssembly

dimensions.title: Mechanisms and rough edges
dimensions.summary: You want to understand memory layout and lifecycle behavior, alongside getting code to run. You also care about idiomatic Rust and overlooked edge cases, so your reviews reach beyond basic functionality.

evidence.quote: Draw me an ASCII diagram of what Rc<RefCell<T>> looks like in memory
oh it was the requestAnimationFrame closure being dropped. why does that happen?
I rewrote my todo app with clap. can you review it and point out non-idiomatic parts?
here is my AABB function, any edge cases I missed?

dimensions.title: Practice with a feedback loop
dimensions.summary: You turn explanations into exercises, quizzes, and working projects. You seek targeted explanations of mistakes and ask for a roadmap, suggesting that you want both immediate feedback and direction for what comes next.

evidence.quote: ok I think I get it. can you give me 3 small exercises about lifetimes?
what should I learn next to get better at game dev in Rust? give me a roadmap
what did I get wrong? explain the ones I missed

traits.name: You keep the keyboard
traits.description: You repeatedly ask for explanations, steps, and review while reserving the implementation for yourself.

evidence.quote: Don't write it for me, just give me the steps.
don't fix them, just tell me
explain AABB first, then let me try to implement it

traits.name: You interrogate the mechanism
traits.description: You follow explanations with questions about how the underlying system behaves, especially when its rules seem surprising.

evidence.quote: so RefCell moves the borrow check to runtime? that feels dangerous, why is it allowed?
explain async/await in Rust vs JavaScript. why does Rust need an executor?
oh it was the requestAnimationFrame closure being dropped. why does that happen?

traits.name: You revisit working code
traits.description: You ask whether your implementations are idiomatic, logically sound, and resilient to edge cases. Getting something running opens another round of questions.

evidence.quote: here's my answer to exercise 1, is it idiomatic?
I replaced the unwraps with ? and a custom error enum. better?
here is my AABB function, any edge cases I missed?

traits.name: You test your understanding
traits.description: You deliberately create opportunities to attempt an answer and discover what you missed, using exercises and quizzes alongside project work.

evidence.quote: can you give me 3 small exercises about lifetimes?
quiz me on Rust traits, 5 questions, wait for my answers
what did I get wrong? explain the ones I missed
